newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak leading shares end week steady and quiet.
newsitem.headline: Slovak leading shares end week steady and quiet.

text.p: The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) closed the week flat on Friday, with most leading Slovak shares remaining illiquid and the 16-share SAX index edging up 0.27 points.
"The market remains illiquid and we saw only a little trading on Friday," Radovan Dzugas of Creditanstalt said.
"We can't say there is no interest in shares at all, but virtually only VSZ is able to match deals during this period," he added.
Steel maker VSZ traded 1,127 shares, closing unchanged at 750 crowns.
But Dzugas said some signs of interest appeared also in other major issues, such as oil refinery Slovnaft, although traded volumes remained insignificant.
"From time to time, we also see speculative deals in Nafta or VUB bank, showing that there is still a possibility of revival," he added.
Overall volume eased to 168,577 shares, from 940,563 shares traded on Thursday, while turnover fell to 86.24 million crowns, from 457.34 million.
